tags.name: Ada K. Damon
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-15: 84ft two-masted Grand Banks fishing schooner, converted for sand-hauling, wrecked Dec 26 1909 during 'Great Christmas Snowstorm' at Steep Hill Beach, Crane Beach, Ipswich. Builder name varies by source (Ebenezer Burnham vs H.A. Burnham, both Essex MA boat builders -- sources agree on Essex, MA). Intertidal wreck visible at low tide, more archaeological site than diving destination; not submerged, snorkeling/masks prohibited by Trustees of Reservations.

tags.name: Wanderer
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-15: Last whaling bark to depart New Bedford on a whaling voyage, 116ft wooden bark built 1878 at Mattapoisett. Grounded on Middle Ground shoal west side of Cuttyhunk Island; anchor chain parted in a gale after departing for her final voyage. Sources conflict on exact date -- the Vineyard Gazette's contemporary Aug 26 1924 report vs. modern retrospectives (WBUR/The Public's Radio) citing Aug 27, 1924. Completely broken up, only small artifacts remain among rocks. Maximum depth 20 feet (6m). Easy dive.

tags.name: SS James Longstreet
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-15: Liberty ship (hull 112), built by Todd Houston Shipbuilding, Houston TX, keel laid 24 Aug 1942, launched 31 Oct 1942, length 441ft6in, beam 57ft, 7,000 DWT (Wikipedia). Grounded/declared total loss Oct 26 1943, acquired by Navy June 1944, scuttled April 25 1945 as target ship (Project Dove / air-to-surface missile testing) on New Found Shoal, Cape Cod Bay, off Eastham. Hulk submerged further in 1996 storm; now lies in ~6-8m. mass.gov's page states differing figures (length 417.7ft, sinking listed as 1950) that conflict with Wikipedia and South Wellfleet local history (441.5ft, scuttled 1945) -- treating Wikipedia + South Wellfleet as the stronger corroborated pair. OSM tags 'access:no'. Unexploded ordnance present — diving not recommended without official clearance.

tags.name: Avery Ledge

Sources (ecdivers.com, idivenewengland.com, scubadiving.com) confirm a year-round harbor/gray seal colony at the adjacent Dry Salvages -- that fact is attributable to Dry Salvages, not confirmed at Avery Ledge itself. tags.name: SS Pendleton
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-15: CORRECTED build year -- Wikipedia and mass.gov both confirm the Pendleton was built in 1944 (not 1942 as previously recorded) by Kaiser Company at the Swan Island Yard, Portland, Oregon. 504-foot Type T2-SE-A1 tanker, beam 68.2ft, 10,448 GRT. Broke in two at 05:40 Feb 18 1952 in a nor'easter (60-70ft seas) six miles off Chatham. Stern grounded off Monomoy Island at 41°35'10"N 69°57'45"W; bow grounded on Pollock Rip Shoal. Famous Finest Hours Coast Guard rescue. Massachusetts BUAR Exempted Site.

tags.name: Frances
tags.notes: Validated 2026-08-15: Frances was a German iron-hulled bark driven ashore during a December gale in 1872 at Head of the Meadow Beach, North Truro (coordinates confirm North Truro, not Wellfleet as a prior draft stated). Carried a cargo of sugar and tin. All crew were rescued by U.S. Life-Saving Service men, who dragged a whaleboat overland from the bay side to the outer beach; the German captain survived the wreck but died several days later from exposure and is buried in North Truro. Bow silhouette still visible at low tide (legendsofamerica.com, islands.com, nps.gov guide). Intertidal/archaeological site, not a conventional dive.

tags.name: U.S.S Yankee Exempt Site
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-15: USS Yankee (1892), 406.1-foot iron auxiliary cruiser, 6,225 ton displacement, built Newport News Shipbuilding & Drydock Co. 1892. Originally Southern Pacific passenger liner El Norte, acquired by Navy April 1898. Grounded on Spindle Rock near Hen and Chickens lightship September 23, 1908 (dense fog + wildfire smoke); refloated Dec 4, 1908 by Arbuckle Wrecking Co.; sank while under tow to New Bedford -- sources place the sinking itself on the night of Dec 4 into Dec 5, 1908. 3 miles east of Round Hill Point, South Dartmouth. Wreck later dynamited as navigation hazard, salvaged for boilers/equipment. Massachusetts BUAR Exempted Site.

tags.description: WWII US Navy minesweeper ran aground on reef and destroyed
tags.name: USS Grouse (AMS-15)
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-15 (confirmed, no corrections needed): WWII wooden minesweeper YMS-321/AMS-15, 136ft, 270 tons displacement, built by Al Larson Boat Building, Terminal Island CA; laid down Aug 29 1942, launched Feb 20 1943. Grounded on Little Salvages off Rockport ~2AM September 21, 1963 during a training exercise; crew evacuated by helicopter, tow attempts failed. Destroyed by Navy explosives September 28, 1963 (confirmed NOT fire). Wreck in ~6m (20ft) water near the California wreck. Massachusetts BUAR Exempted Site.

tags.name: California
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-15 (confirmed, no corrections needed): Boston beam trawler, 104.1ft length, 82 GRT, built 1917 in Boston MA, owned by Matteo Logrande, hailing from Gloucester. Foundered September 15, 1955 between Little Salvages and Dry Salvages, ~42°40'25"N 70°34'19"W. Massachusetts BUAR Exempted Site. Year-round harbor/gray seal colony documented at the adjacent Dry Salvages (ecdivers.com, idivenewengland.com, scubadiving.com) -- seals are commonly seen by divers in the area though not confirmed feeding/hauling on the wreck itself.

tags.name: Charles S. Haight
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-15: CORRECTED location -- prior note incorrectly placed this wreck near Graves Ledge; it actually grounded on the Flat Ground inside the Dry Salvages, ~1.5 miles east of Rockport (not Graves Ledge, which is near Boston Harbor). Liberty ship, builder J.A. Jones Construction Co., Brunswick GA, laid down 15 Aug 1944, completed 3 Oct 1944. Grounded overnight April 1-2, 1946 while in ballast from Newport, England to New York, driven inshore by SE winds in poor visibility. Sources disagree on exact dimensions: Wikipedia gives length 441ft6in / 7,176 GRT; harbormasters.org gives 422.8ft / 7,198 GRT -- both are cited pending further reconciliation. Only the triple-expansion steam engine remains clearly visible, marked by Red Nun '2'. Massachusetts BUAR Exempted Site.

tags.description: 1890s cargo steamship that was abandoned and left to sink
tags.name: City of Taunton
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-15 (confirmed, no corrections needed): Freight sidepaddle (sidewheel) steamship, 292 feet length, built 1892 in Chelsea MA by Montgomery & Howard. Served the Fall River Line freight fleet. Grounded and abandoned at Brayton Point, Somerset MA in the 1930s as the Fall River Line collapsed. Wreck visible at low tide on the western shore of Mount Hope Bay at 41°42'35.48"N 71°10'42.58"W.

tags.name: Green Jacket Shoal
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-15: Rhode Island's largest ship graveyard — 33-acre shoal in the Providence River between Providence and East Providence with 29 confirmed wrecks (URI marine archaeologist David Robinson). Named for local term for the eelgrass ('green jacket') once covering the shoal. Vessel-class breakdown varies slightly by source (URI/Wikipedia vs. regional press) but both agree on ~29 total including the sidewheel steamboats Bay Queen and Mount Hope. CRMC designated it a Marine Protected Area in 2018 (confirmed via crmc.ri.gov) with restricted access enforced by RI DEM, State Police, and East Providence harbormaster. Not accessible to recreational divers. Boat tours via Providence River Boat Company.

tags.name: Brenton Reef
tags.notes: Re-audited 2026-08-15 (confirmed, no corrections needed): LV-39 lightship, wooden vessel 119ft 6in length, 387 gross tons, built ~1875. Stationed at Brenton Reef 1897-1935. Struck by USS Iowa August 1905 (part of stem carried away, no lives lost). Sank 1975 while under tow to Beverly MA. First dived July 5, 2004 by Bob Foster, David Caldwell, Heather Knowles. Rests upright with a port list; sources give depth as 175-180ft (53-55m), 20-25ft relief. Technical dive only (trimix/advanced tech cert required).
